name: Extreme heat
summary: Queensland's severe heatwave warning ended on 19 Nov; Philippine danger-level heat indices are local; no deadly heatwave
state: The Bureau of Meteorology's severe heatwave warning for Far North Queensland ran only to 19 Nov, after Weipa logged 41 straight days above 36°C (The Watchers). PAGASA forecast danger-level heat indices of 42–44°C at eight Philippine stations on 18 Nov, mainly in Palawan, Eastern Samar and Mindanao (GMA News), a local rather than regional warning. Searches on 21 Nov found no current heatwave warning across a major region, no new national record and no deadly heatwave, so the level falls to Normal.
for_you: No major heatwave warnings are in force. Southern-hemisphere summer is starting, so heat warnings in Australia, southern Africa and South America tend to rise from December; follow national weather services if travelling.
rubric_hit: Normal: no heatwave warnings across a major region on 21 Nov; Queensland severe warning ended 19 Nov

why: Heat is the deadliest weather hazard globally, straining power grids, crops and health systems.
drivers: Heat domes, climate warming, season, humidity, urban heat islands.

rubric.alert: Deadly heatwave with top-tier official warnings across a large population.
rubric.watch: Heatwave warnings across a major region, or national temperature records.
rubric.normal: No major heatwaves affecting large populations.
